original_value: Many advanced satellite estimation methods have been developed, but global forest aboveground biomass (AGB) products remain largely uncertain. In this study, we explored data fusion techniques to generate a global forest AGB map for the 2000s at 0.01-degree resolution with improved accuracy by integrating ten existing local or global maps. The error removal and simple averaging algorithm, which is efficient and makes no assumption about the data and associated errors, was proposed to integrate these ten forest AGB maps. We first compiled the global reference AGB from in situ measurements and high-resolution AGB data that were originally derived from field data and airborne lidar data and determined the errors of each forest AGB map at the pixels with corresponding reference AGB values. Based on the errors determined from reference AGB data, the pixel-by-pixel errors associated with each of the ten AGB datasets were estimated from multiple predictors (e.g., leaf area index, forest canopy height, forest cover, land surface elevation, slope, temperature, and precipitation) using the random forest algorithm. The estimated pixel-by-pixel errors were then removed from the corresponding forest AGB datasets, and finally, global forest AGB maps were generated by combining the calibrated existing forest AGB datasets using the simple averaging algorithm. Cross-validation using reference AGB data showed that the accuracy of the fused global forest AGB map had an R-squared of 0.61 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 53.68 Mg/ha, which is better than the reported accuracies (R-squared of 0.56 and RMSE larger than 80 Mg/ha) in the literature. Intercomparison with previous studies also suggested that the fused AGB estimates were much closer to the reference AGB values. This study attempted to integrate existing forest AGB datasets for generating a global forest AGB map with better accuracy and moved one step forward for our understanding of the global terrestrial carbon cycle by providing improved benchmarks of global forest carbon stocks.

result.paraphrase: Although many advanced satellite-based estimation methods have been developed, global forest aboveground biomass (AGB) products are still highly uncertain. Here, we used data fusion to create an improved global forest AGB map for the 2000s at 0.01-degree resolution by combining ten existing local and global maps. To merge these datasets, we proposed an efficient error-removal plus simple-averaging approach that makes no assumptions about the data or their associated errors. We first assembled global reference AGB from in situ measurements and high-resolution AGB data originally derived from field observations and airborne lidar, then quantified each forest AGB map’s errors at pixels with matching reference values. Using those reference-based errors, we estimated pixel-level errors for each of the ten AGB datasets from multiple predictors, including leaf area index, forest canopy height, forest cover, land surface elevation, slope, temperature, and precipitation, with the random forest algorithm. The estimated pixel-by-pixel errors were then removed from the corresponding forest AGB datasets, and the calibrated products were finally combined with simple averaging to generate global forest AGB maps. Cross-validation against reference AGB data showed that the fused map achieved an R-squared of 0.61 and an RMSE of 53.68 Mg/ha, outperforming previously reported accuracies (R-squared of 0.56 and RMSE above 80 Mg/ha). Comparisons with earlier studies also indicated that the fused AGB estimates were much closer to the reference AGB values. Overall, this work integrated existing forest AGB datasets to produce a more accurate global forest AGB map and advanced understanding of the global terrestrial carbon cycle by providing improved benchmarks for global forest carbon stocks.
